title: Ben Affleck Harnesses AI for Multiple Roles in Netflix’s New Film “Animals,” Reports Hollywood Reporter
body:
Ben Affleck revealed that artificial‑intelligence tools were woven into multiple stages of production for his upcoming Netflix thriller Animals, sparking fresh debate about how Hollywood’s biggest stars and studios are embracing the technology. Speaking at Bloomberg’s 2026 Screentime conference, the Oscar‑winning actor‑director admitted that AI was used “for lots of things” on the film, though he stopped short of naming specific applications. The comments come as Netflix recently invested roughly $600 million in an AI‑focused media startup, underscoring the streaming giant’s commitment to integrating generative technology into its content pipeline.

Affleck’s remarks mark one of the most high‑profile acknowledgments of AI’s role in a mainstream feature to date. While he declined to detail the exact processes, industry insiders suggest the tools could have been employed for script analysis, visual effects pre‑visualization, virtual set extensions, and even post‑production editing. “We’re experimenting with AI‑driven storyboards and location scouting,” a crew member, who asked to remain anonymous, told Bloomberg. “It speeds up the creative workflow, but it also forces us to rethink how we collaborate with machines.” The actor’s candidness reflects a broader shift among filmmakers who are moving from cautious curiosity to active adoption of generative models for everything from dialogue polishing to sound design.

The Netflix‑Affleck partnership arrives at a moment when the streaming platform is aggressively expanding its AI portfolio. Earlier this year, Netflix poured a six‑figure sum into a startup that builds synthetic‑voice and deep‑fake technologies for dubbing and localization, aiming to cut the time and cost of delivering content in multiple languages. Analysts see the $600 million infusion as a strategic bet that AI will become a cost‑saving engine for the ever‑growing library of original titles. “If you can generate a believable background crowd or a realistic animal CG element without a full VFX house, you shave millions off the budget,” noted media‑tech analyst Priya Desai of TechScope. “Affleck’s film could be a test case for how far that can go without compromising quality.”

Critics, however, warn that the rush to embed AI could raise ethical and creative concerns. Unions representing writers, editors, and visual‑effects artists have voiced apprehension that generative tools might erode job security and dilute artistic authorship. The Writers Guild of America recently filed a petition urging studios to establish clear guidelines for AI‑assisted script work, arguing that credit and compensation frameworks must evolve alongside the technology. In response, Netflix’s chief content officer, Kelly Bennett, emphasized that the company “will continue to work with guilds to ensure AI augments, not replaces, human talent.” Whether that promise will hold as AI capabilities expand remains an open question.

From a commercial standpoint, the integration of AI could influence the film’s market performance. Netflix’s data‑driven approach already tailors marketing pushes based on viewer behavior; adding AI‑generated assets—such as dynamic trailers that adapt to individual user preferences—could further amplify reach. If Animals delivers a compelling thriller experience while showcasing AI‑enhanced production values, it may set a precedent for future collaborations between A‑list talent and algorithmic tools. Conversely, any perceivable drop in quality or a backlash over perceived “machine‑made” content could prompt a reevaluation of the technology’s role in high‑budget cinema.

As the premiere of Animals looms, the industry will be watching not only for the film’s artistic merits but also for the practical outcomes of its AI‑heavy workflow. Affleck’s openness about using the technology may encourage other filmmakers to experiment, while also prompting regulators and guilds to refine the rules governing its use. In the months ahead, the success—or failure—of this experiment could shape the next wave of Hollywood production, determining whether AI becomes a silent partner behind blockbuster storytelling or a controversial shortcut that reshapes the creative labor landscape.
